script.base: Spread and total are not in the pack, so this script is form-only, not a market read. Over weeks 1-2 CIN's pass game has run through Tee Higgins (16.0 targets, 154 yards, 210 air yards) ahead of Ja'Marr Chase (13.0/87/115), with Chase Brown at 36.0 carries for 136 yards, while Burrow is +0.27 EPA/dropback when not blitzed. pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost because two games overstated the roles. Higgins' 154 yards were one explosive afternoon, and Pittsburgh's 25% blitz plus Burrow's -0.62 EPA versus blitz turned this into quick throws, so 54.5 missed. Warren, a 10.5-carry committee back, absorbed Dowdle's share once PIT protected a lead the missing spread might have implied, and 15 carries at his 4.24 YPC cleared 58 even though CIN had allowed only 4 runs of 10+ through two weeks. No inactives and no weather means a late OL or RB scratch, or wind that was never in the pack, could have rewritten both legs.
slip_story: One story: CIN's offense functions in its weeks 1-2 shape (Higgins is the downfield target, Burrow is not blitzed into a stall) and PIT does not grind Warren into a 15-carry game. Higgins recyds over 54.5 and Warren rushyds under 58 win together in that base script and in the CIN-ahead flip; both lose if PIT blitzes Burrow and then runs. Not a shootout stack, and not a total under mixed with overs.
